name: Standard ML
note: standardization began in 1983; its formal Definition was published in 1990
typeSystem: Static, strong, Hindley-Milner type inference with parametric polymorphism, algebraic datatypes, and pattern matching, plus an explicit module system (structures, signatures, and functors) and a fully formal semantics published as 'The Definition of Standard ML'.
runtime: Compiled to native code by most modern implementations; some provide an interactive, incremental top-level for exploratory development alongside batch compilation.

runtimes.name: SML/NJ
runtimes.role: Influential optimizing implementation with an interactive top level and native code generation.

runtimes.name: MLton
runtimes.role: Whole-program optimising compiler that produces highly efficient native binaries.

runtimes.name: PolyML
runtimes.role: Fast native-code implementation, widely used to host the Isabelle and HOL4 theorem provers.

compilers.name: SML/NJ
compilers.role: Influential optimizing compiler and interactive top level.

compilers.name: PolyML
compilers.role: Native-code compiler, often embedded inside other tools.

concurrencyModel: Implementation-dependent: Poly/ML provides OS-level parallel threads; SML/NJ's Concurrent ML and MLton provide user-level concurrency.

codeExample.caption: Hello, World! plus a recursive factorial
codeExample.source:
fun fact 0 = 1
  | fact n = n * fact (n - 1)

val () = print (Int.toString (fact 10) ^ "\n")
